sources.entry: A document management system (DMS) is a system used to receive, track, manage and store documents and reduce paper.

summary.name: Document management system
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing document management systems (DMS): computerized systems for storing, sharing, tracking and managing electronic files, with version tracking and related concepts.
use_cases: understanding how document management systems work
comparing DMS features such as versioning and workflow
learning about document control for regulated industries
reducing paper filing with electronic storage
summary.what_it_does: The article explains what a document management system is and how it stores, shares, tracks and manages electronic documents, including version and revision history. It gives a brief history from 1980s imaging systems through enterprise content management. It describes core components such as metadata, OCR capture, indexing, retrieval, security and access control, workflow, collaboration, versioning and search. It also covers document control requirements in regulated industries and lists relevant ISO standards.
notable: Describes DMS components in a detailed capability table (metadata, OCR capture, indexing, retrieval, workflow, versioning)
Covers document control requirements in regulated industries such as medical devices, food safety and healthcare
Lists relevant ISO standards including ISO 15489 records management and ISO 32000 PDF
caveats: This is an encyclopedia overview, not a specific software product, so it names no product's pricing or platforms
Some historical and standards claims are cited to sources and may be dated
